rounds.text: Ekam Leasing And Finance Co Ltd is showing clear, quantifiable signs of a powerful operational turnaround that the market has yet to fully appreciate [E52]. Trailing twelve-month sales growth has surged to 56% [E16], backed by rules-based screen metrics showing a dramatic year-on-year sales increase of 517% [E47] and net profit growth of 680% [E49]. This fundamental acceleration is reflected in the company's recent performance scores, which rank results at 95 out of 100 while market sentiment and price remain cautious [E52]. Share price momentum is already beginning to validate this inflection, delivering a 35% return over the past year [E21] and holding comfortably near its 52-week range at 83% of capacity [E4]. Furthermore, the valuation remains remarkably modest, trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 1.30x on a book value of ₹ 6.40 [E1] and closely tracking the sector benchmark P/B of 1.37x [E6]. Conceded: long-term compounded sales growth over the past three, five, and ten years remains negative [E13, E14, E15], reflecting the painful legacy of prior downturns that the current explosive growth is only just beginning to reverse [E52].

Ekam Leasing And Finance Co Ltd carries severe fundamental risks that are masked by short-term speculative momentum. The company exhibits catastrophic profitability metrics, featuring a trailing twelve-month ROE of -107.02% and an ROCE of -70.68%, both dramatically worse than sector benchmarks [E8, E9]. Operational destruction is evident as the operating margin collapsed to -1436% in the TTM, plunging 1503 percentage points compared to three years earlier [E26]. Furthermore, core business contraction is structural, demonstrated by compounded sales growth of -51% over three years and -31% over five years [E14, E15]. Cash generation has completely broken down, resulting in negative operating cash flow and free cash flow of Rs -0.88 Cr each for Mar 2026, alongside a weak current ratio of 0.93x where current liabilities exceed current assets [E32, E34]. Finally, low promoter holding at 27.70% and flagged low interest coverage add substantial governance and solvency hazards [E42, E44]. Conceded: [E16].

The bear points to catastrophic trailing ROE and ROCE metrics [E8, E9], but dismisses the explosive turnaround captured by recent operational catalysts, including trailing twelve-month sales growth of 56% and screen flags of YoY sales accelerating by 517% alongside net profit surging 680% [E16, E47, E49]. Conceded: [E26]. While the bear highlights long-term sales contraction [E14, E15], it ignores the explicit bias check warning against dismissing a fundamental turnaround where results score 95 out of 100 on accelerating momentum while sentiment stays cautious [E52]. The bear's structural cash flow critique based on Mar 2026 [E32] overlooks that promoter holding has remained fully stable at 27.70% through recent periods [E37], showing insider commitment during the transition. Finally, although current liabilities exceed assets [E34], debt to equity remains at a manageable 0.49x representing moderate leverage [E33].

The bull points to recent operational catalysts including TTM sales growth and screen flags of YoY sales and net profit surges [E16, E47, E49], but these co-exist with a catastrophic compounded sales contraction of -51% over 3 years and -31% over 5 years [E14, E15, E43], proving that short-term spikes emerge from a deeply depressed historical base. Conceded: [E52]. The bull cites the insider-bias check warning against dismissing a fundamental turnaround score of 95 out of 100 [E52], but this ignores the stark reality that compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months stands at an abysmal -255% [E17] and operating margins have collapsed by an astonishing -1503 percentage points [E26]. While the bull claims stable promoter holding at 27.70% [E37] shows commitment, this level is explicitly flagged as a negative low promoter holding [E44] alongside severe structural deterioration such as negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -0.88 Cr [E31, E32] and a low interest coverage ratio warning [E42]. Finally, the bull dismisses liquidity strains by pointing to a moderate 0.49x debt-to-equity ratio [E33], ignoring the vulnerable balance sheet reality where current liabilities explicitly exceed current assets with a current ratio of 0.93x [E34], alongside persistent negative returns on equity reaching -70% [E25, E51].
